Biomax Peptides

27 /100
Low Transparency
HPLC and MS testing are claimed on the homepage, but no COA is publicly posted anywhere on the site. COAs are "available upon request" only. The domain launched December 2024, leaving no community track record to draw on. Most process claims cannot be independently confirmed from public materials.

Third-Party Testing Practice
The homepage states "HPLC and mass spectrometry verified" as a feature claim. However, no COA is publicly posted anywhere on the site - not on product pages, not in a dedicated lab results section, and not in the footer. The "Certificates of Analysis (COAs) - Available upon request" line confirms testing is claimed but documentation is not proactively shared. Frequency, catalog coverage, and the name of any testing lab are entirely absent from public materials. Credit given for the explicit method claim; significant deduction for no public documentation to confirm it.

What Drives the Score
The gap between claimed and documented
Biomax Peptides makes specific testing claims - HPLC, mass spectrometry, 99% purity minimum - and makes them publicly, on the homepage. That's more than some vendors do. The problem is that nothing behind those claims is publicly verifiable. No COA archive, no product-page documentation, no lab name, no batch numbers. "Available upon request" means a stranger must initiate contact before any documentation is reachable. Under the VTS rubric, that structure scores near the bottom on five of seven dimensions, regardless of whether the underlying testing is real.
Policy is a genuine bright spot
The refund and shipping pages are unusually specific for a vendor at this transparency tier. Cancellation terms, damage reporting windows, the 3.8% cancellation fee, and international shipping caveats are all clearly stated and publicly accessible without any account or login. That earns near-full marks on Policy Transparency - the one dimension where Biomax outperforms vendors scoring significantly higher overall.
What a score revision would require
Publishing COAs publicly - even a representative sample per product with lot numbers and the issuing lab identified - would move COA Accessibility from 6 to 12, unlock meaningful points in Traceability and Completeness, and make Recency assessable. That single structural change would push the score into the Limited band. Time in market will improve the Operational Track Record score as the operation establishes a community presence.
Community Signal - Separate Field
Independent Test Results
No community-commissioned independent test results identified in public forums as of August 2026.
Community Experience
No reviews found on Trustpilot, Reddit, or peptide forums as of mid-2026 per multiple independent review sources. The vendor's domain name (biomaxpeptides.com) is noted to cause confusion with similarly named but unrelated operations (biomax.ca, biomaxx.shop). The Facebook and Instagram links in the site footer point to "CA Hormones" accounts rather than a Biomax-branded presence, suggesting a possible prior operating identity. Self-reported address is 127 E 18th St, Costa Mesa, CA -- listed on the site but unverifiable from public records due to private WHOIS registration.
